title: Bind local folder operations to the selected directory identity
context: A Windows selection kept an entire read-only shared directory chain alive. On standard-user Win11, atomic replacements of direct child CSVs failed while the application was idle. Source operations still require the original selected root, catalogued parents, validated bytes and an active grant.
decision: Retain a handle to the selected root for identity, using metadata-only access with full sharing on Windows. At each source operation, reopen from the filesystem root one component at a time without following reparse points, and compare the selected root and catalogued parent identities. Keep the Windows chain and verified file handles through source I/O and final commit. Compare identities of open handles, using Windows volume serial numbers and 128-bit file IDs. Reject replacements of directories under the old scope and allow files at existing catalog paths to be reread and reviewed by digest.
authority: ADR 0007 delegates engineering choices. M1-008 calls for ordinary external saves between reads, preservation of native scope and independent standard-user Windows verification.

alternatives.option: Continue to pin all ancestors while a selection is live.
alternatives.reason: The observed Windows sharing rules prevent common atomic saves under the selected root.

alternatives.option: Store an absolute path and open it directly for later reads.
alternatives.reason: Path spelling alone cannot distinguish a replacement directory or a reparse-point redirection.

consequences: The reviewed mapping association remains canonical and path-based. Native object identity is session-scoped. Previously accepted frozen bytes are independent of the external folder.

ScopeHub releases the strict handles between filesystem operations. A conflicting mutation during Windows source verification can fail, and a filesystem that cannot supply the required object identity fails closed.
Folder refresh must enumerate through a verified root and revalidate the reviewed membership and digests against the live source. Directory pins alone do not freeze child membership.
revisit_when: A supported filesystem needs a different reliable identity mechanism, or a source workflow requires snapshot semantics for an entire directory.
